title: Sell Mineral Rights in Lower Burrell, PA
primaryKeyword: sell mineral rights lower burrell pa
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Lower Burrell, PA
metaDescription: Lower Burrell, an urbanized small city in Westmoreland County, still carries wet-gas Marcellus mineral rights under residential and vacant lots.
heroLead: Lower Burrell is one of the more urbanized parts of Westmoreland County, and mineral ownership under its residential streets is often more complicated than people expect.
intro: As farmland around Lower Burrell filled in with subdivisions and small commercial strips over the decades, mineral rights didn't always follow the surface the same way twice. Some parcels conveyed everything together; others reserved oil and gas separately, sometimes to a different family branch entirely. Untangling that on an urbanized city lot takes the same careful courthouse work as a rural farm tract, even though the surface looks nothing alike.

sections.heading: Urban Lots, Rural-Era Deeds
paragraphs: A lot of Lower Burrell's residential streets sit on land that was still farmland within living memory, and the deed reservations from that transition are what actually control mineral ownership today, regardless of what's been built on the surface since.

Lower Burrell's transition from farmland to small city happened gradually enough that some of the original farm-family names still appear on mineral records for parcels their descendants haven't lived on in decades.

sections.heading: Westmoreland's Wet-Gas Value Under a City
paragraphs: Being surrounded by development doesn't remove the wet-gas value from the Marcellus shale under Lower Burrell — it just means a well is more likely to be sited on nearby open ground and reach the minerals horizontally rather than drilling directly through a residential block.

sections.heading: What We Check on an Urbanized Parcel
paragraphs: We pull the deed history back through the property's transition from farmland to developed lot, confirm whether minerals were reserved, and check for any unit or lease activity nearby through the Westmoreland County recorder's office.

faqs.question: Can a city lot in Lower Burrell really carry mineral value?
faqs.answer: Yes, if minerals were reserved at some point in the deed chain, that value doesn't disappear just because the surface became residential.

faqs.question: Would drilling ever happen directly in a Lower Burrell neighborhood?
faqs.answer: Unlikely — modern horizontal wells are typically sited on open ground nearby and reach minerals under developed areas without surface disturbance there.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my city lot has mineral rights attached?
faqs.answer: We pull the recorded deed chain from the Westmoreland County courthouse to see exactly what was reserved or conveyed.

faqs.question: Would a buyer really be interested in a residential city lot's minerals?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the deed shows minerals were reserved rather than conveyed with the surface — lot size and current use don't determine whether an interest is worth evaluating.
